serviceContent.title: TDS on Expense
serviceContent.description: Track and manage TDS deductions on every expense with ease

trackData.title: Start Definition
trackData.desc: TDS requires the payer to deduct tax while making certain business payments and deposit that tax to the government. It helps ensure income reporting at the source and prevents under-reporting.

trackData.title: Why It Matters for Effortless Users
trackData.desc: Effortless automatically applies the correct TDS section, rate, and threshold based on the expense type and vendor PAN status. This eliminates manual mistakes and reduces audit exposure.

serviceContent.title: Key Factors
keyFactor: TDS depends on the nature of the expense (not vendor)
Rates may vary for Individual vs Non-Individual vendors
Thresholds may apply per transaction or cumulative FY basis
PAN not linked to Aadhaar → TDS @ 20% applies

serviceContent.description: Designed to match the pace of growing teams and their needs.

tdsFAQ.question: Does Effortless automatically calculate TDS?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. Effortless uses the configured TDS sections and rates based on Tax behaviour mapping during setup process to automatically compute TDS on eligible transactions.

tdsFAQ.question: Can we define multiple TDS sections for one vendor?
tdsFAQ.answer: TDS mapping is done at Expense GL level and not at vendor level. You can map multiple Expense GL at the time of bill booking which inturn maps the respective TDS tagged under multiple GL's to the same vendor and select the relevant one at the time of transaction Booking.

tdsFAQ.question: Can the system handle 'No PAN' higher rate deduction (20%)?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. Effortless automatically applies the higher rate if vendor PAN is not captured.

tdsFAQ.question: At what stage is TDS calculated – at Bill Booking or Payment?
tdsFAQ.answer: For Bill Booking – TDS is deducted when the liability is recorded. For Vendor Advance Payment Level – TDS is deducted only when payment is made.

tdsFAQ.question: Does the system generate TDS Challan?
tdsFAQ.answer: No. Effortless does not generate a TDS challan.

tdsFAQ.question: Can we get TDS computation reports section-wise, vendor-wise, and period-wise?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. Effortless provides detailed reports for: Section-wise summary Vendor-wise deduction register Periodic (monthly/quarterly) compliance view

tdsFAQ.question: Can Effortless generate Form 26Q/27Q data for quarterly filing?
tdsFAQ.answer: No. But You can export a clean TDS Report, which can be used for TDS filing with minimal modifications (as per RPU/NSDL format).

tdsFAQ.question: Can Effortless validate TDS with Form 26AS?
tdsFAQ.answer: Currently, direct 26AS reconciliation is not available, but you can export TDS data and reconcile externally. (Planned feature: Automated 26AS match.)

tdsFAQ.question: Does Effortless deduct TDS only on the excess amount over threshold or the entire amount?
tdsFAQ.answer: As per the Income-tax Act, once the cumulative payments to a deductee exceed the prescribed threshold in a financial year, TDS is deducted on the entire amount of the transaction that crosses the threshold, not just on the excess. Effortless following this exactly once threshold is breached, the entire bill amount on which TDS is applicable will be considered for deduction.

serviceContent.title: GST Input Tax Credit (ITC)
serviceContent.description: Track and claim your eligible GST credits accurately.

trackData.title: What is Input Tax Credit (ITC)
trackData.desc: Input Tax Credit (ITC) allows a registered business to reduce its GST liability by claiming credit for the GST paid on purchases of goods or services that are used in the course of business. In simple terms, ITC ensures tax is paid only on the value added at each stage of the supply chain.

trackData.title: Example
trackData.desc: If a business pays ₹18,000 GST on purchases and collects ₹25,000 GST on sales, it can claim ₹18,000 as ITC and remit only ₹7,000 to the government.

serviceContent.title: Basic Conditions for
serviceContent.description: To avail ITC, the following conditions must be satisfied
tdsAutomation: The taxpayer must be registered under GST
The invoice or debit note must be available and contain all prescribed details
The supplier must have uploaded the invoice in their GSTR-1 and paid tax to the government (appearing in the recipient's GSTR-2B)
Goods or services must be received and used for business purposes
The payment to the supplier (including tax) must be made within 180 days of invoice date
ITC must be claimed within the due date for the September return following the end of the financial year (or annual return filing, whichever is earlier)

tdsFAQ.question: Does Effortless auto-calculate eligible ITC?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. It reads GST rates from supplier invoices and segregates taxable, exempt, and reverse-charge items.

tdsFAQ.question: Can reports be viewed vendor-wise and period-wise?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. Detailed GST Input Summary and Mismatch Report are available.

tdsFAQ.question: Does Effortless handle reverse charge ITC?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. The system flags RCM entries separately and credits them only once payment of tax is confirmed in books.

tdsFAQ.question: Can client customize input credit eligibility basis the industry
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes, they can customise at each expense category level.

serviceContent.title: Cost Centre
serviceContent.description: Track and manage expenses by department or project

trackData.title: What is a Cost Centre
trackData.desc:
A Cost Centre is a unit within an organization for which costs and revenues can be tracked separately. It helps management understand where money is being earned or spent and analyze profitability by department, project, branch, or business vertical.
In accounting systems, cost centers act as analytical dimensions used to allocate income and expenses accurately across various business activities.

serviceContent.title: Purpose of
serviceContent.description: To monitor, control, and analyze expenses for specific departments, teams, or projects.
tdsAutomation: To identify which segment or department is generating profit or incurring losses
To support budgeting, variance analysis, and management reporting
To help link operational activities with financial outcomes
To enable multi-dimensional analysis, such as project-wise or location-wise cost tracking

serviceContent.title: Examples of
serviceContent.description: A company tracks marketing, sales, and HR expenses separately to measure each department’s spending and performance.

tableBody.examples: Production Unit A, Production Unit B
tableBody.purpose: Track cost and efficiency by plant
Track labour, materials, and overhead project-wise

serviceContent.title: How Cost Centers
serviceContent.description: Effortless automatically tags expenses, invoices, and payments to the right cost centers, giving clear visibility into where money is spent and how each team performs.

tableBody.explanation: Create cost centers in Settings to sync with Tally. Legacy Tally cost centers not imported can be hidden in Effortless.
Users can tag cost centers while booking transactions — e.g., while creating invoices, expenses, reimbursement or bank entries.
Effortless allows grouping under parent and sub-cost centres for better reporting (e.g., 'North India' > 'Delhi Office').
Cost centre tagging is fully synced with Tally so that expenses and incomes remain aligned in both systems.Reports
Detailed cost centre reports show total income, expenses, and net profit by cost centre for any selected period.

tdsFAQ.question: Can one transaction have multiple cost centers?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. Each line item can be tagged to different cost centers.

tdsFAQ.question: Are cost centers mandatory?
tdsFAQ.answer: Optional. They can be enabled as per organization structure.

tdsFAQ.question: Does Effortless sync cost centers with Tally?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. Both creation and tagging are automatically synced.

tdsFAQ.question: Can we view profitability by cost centre?
tdsFAQ.answer: Yes. Reports provide income, expense, and balance summary per cost centre.
